title: Pro cycling transfers 2026/2027: Carapaz to NSN, Ganna to Lidl-Trek, Roglič ponders, Lidl-Trek sweeps up and Picnic lose more riders
content:
Cyclist
Pro cycling transfers 2026/2027: Carapaz to NSN, Ganna to Lidl-Trek, Roglič ponders, Lidl-Trek sweeps up and Picnic lose more riders

Now the racing is pretty much done, the transfer market is hotting up. With hundreds of riders on the men’s and women’s WorldTour requiring a new contract for 2027, there are a lot of deals to be made, whether that’s contract extensions or moves elsewhere.

Some of the biggest names on this year’s market for the men included Richard Carapaz, Jai Hindley, Primož Roglič, Arnaud de Lie and Ben O’Connor. As for the women, Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney, Elisa Balsamo, Cecilie Uttrup Ludwig and Chloé Dygert seem to be the biggest names linked with moves.

Many of those rumours have now been wrapped up, though some futures still hang in the air. Mid-contract transfers have become more prevalent in recent years, and this week has seen three massive moves.

Here are some of the biggest stories we have so far, with some confirmed and some still in the rumour phase.

Confirmed: Richard Carapaz to move to NSN Cycling

Richard Carapaz, winner of two stages and the polka-dot jersey at this year’s Tour de France, has been EF Education-EasyPost’s star boy for four seasons now. During that time, he’s won three Tour de France stages, two polka-dot jerseys, and finished on the podium of the Giro d’Italia. Having underpinned the team’s GC strategy, Carapaz will be exiting the American squad this winter.

The Ecuadorian had a contract for 2027 with EF, but has signed a deal to move to Swiss/Spanish team NSN Cycling. Netcompany Ineos were believed to be in the race for Carapaz’s signature, but NSN won the battle.

The team, backed by Spanish World Cup winner Andres Iniesta, has been explicit about wanting to bolster its GC arsenal for 2027. Recent signings confirm this, with climbers Santiago Buitrago and Lennart Van Eetvelt both secured, who may help back Carapaz for a Giro GC attempt next spring.

Confirmed: Giulio Ciccone to Pinarello-Q36.5

After a season of highs and lows, Giulio Ciccone has confirmed that he will be moving teams in 2027. This will see the end of a seven-year partnership at Lidl-Trek, the only WorldTour team the Italian has raced for.

After a quick turnaround, it emerged that Ciccone would be heading to Tom Pidcock’s Pinarello Q36.5.

Ciccone will spearhead the team’s big transformation in 2027, with WorldTour promotion a key ambition. Ciccone is the 11th rider to pen a deal with Pinarello this year. Among them are Czech sprinter and former Vuelta stage winner Pavel Bittner, American talent AJ August, British Time-Trial Champion Ethan Hayter and Tour stage winner Mauro Schmid.

According to reports, Pinarello have been told that they would be next in line for promotion if any team drops out of the sport’s top division. In recent weeks, it has been speculated that Picnic-PostNL would be demoted in 2028, perhaps voluntarily. If that’s the case, Ciccone could be back on the WorldTour in just a few months.

Confirmed: Fillipo Ganna to Lidl-Trek

Possibly the biggest transfer bomb came this week when it was confirmed that Filippo Ganna would leave Netcompany Ineos after seven years with the team. The Italian was seen to be a totem of Ineos’s line-up in the post-Froome era, having won countless Grand Tour stages and two world titles while riding for the squad. However, Ganna’s future now lies with Lidl-Trek as he has penned a three-year deal.

It’s said that the Ciccone transfer helped to free up resources and space within the team. Lidl-Trek have had an Italian connection for some time, despite a change at the helm this year. The team is also home to the other members of Italy’s golden team pursuit squad in Jonathan Milan and Simone Consonni.

In a statement announcing the news, Ganna mentioned that he wants to place more emphasis on the Classics. The 30-year-old managed to win his first major one-day race this year at Dwars door Vlaanderen, but a pairing with Mads Pedersen could prove interesting in the Classics going forward.

Lidl-Trek are going to have quite the team time-trial roster in 2027 with the likes of Jakob Söderqvist, Mads Pedersen, Derek Gee-West, Juan Ayuso and Jonathan Milan all under one roof.

Rumoured: Primož Roglič’s future unknown

Primož Roglič joined Red Bull in 2024 after leaving Visma-Lease a Bike in the aftermath of a messy Vuelta a España. However, after three years at the German team, during which he won his fourth Vuelta title, it has been confirmed that the Slovenian will be moving at the end of 2026.

Roglič has increased his stock since the move was confimed in August, with a Vuelta podium and European title to come later this year.

The teams vying for the Roglič contract have changed since the announcement came too. Spanish newspaper Marca believes that Bahrain Victorious could be interested in the four-time Vuelta winner. Since the Tour, Het Laatste Nieuws has also reported that both Pinarello Q36.5 and Lotto-Intermarché are interested, with particular interest from the Belgian squad. Tudor Pro Cycling have also been suggested. However it’s unclear who is currently in pole position.

At Il Lombardia last weekend, Roglič hinted that he could actually take the decision to retire. His wife Lora has tried to dissuade him.

‘I have a lot on my mind, and the issue is me,’ Roglič told Slovenian site Siol last week. I have to decide whether to sign or call it a day. Sometimes I lean one way, sometimes the other.’

Rumoured: Tao Geogheghan Hart to EF Education-EasyPost

Lidl-Trek might feel as though this signing hasn’t paid dividends. When the Brit joined the squad in 2024, he was hot off a competitive year in which he could have contended for Giro glory if it wasn’t for a crash.

The move was considered to be one of the biggest transfer stories of the year when it happened but Geoghegan Hart has off the boil since his move to Lidl-Trek. He has only raced one Grand Tour during his three year spell at the team, and he’s failed to reach the top ten at a WorldTour race’s final standings. Crashes and injury can explain a lot of this, but glimmers of another Giro title are nowhere to be seen.

Daniel Benson believes the 2020 Giro champion is set for a move to EF Education-EasyPost in the new year. The deal would see Geoghegan Hart become one of EF’s top climbers, especially after Carapaz’s departure. Whether he has what it takes to turn his GC career around is to be seen.

Speaking of former Ineos riders, Iván Sosa is also linked to EF. The Colombian, who now rides for Equipo Kern Pharma, has been enjoying a decent 2026 season. This move will see him return to the WorldTour after his former wonderkid status in the early 2020s.

Confirmed: Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney leads GC switch-up at Lidl-Trek

Lidl-Trek have been raking in the transfers this year. The men’s and women’s teams have both been incredibly active in the transfer market, with names like Ally Wollaston, Blanka Vas and Jordi Meeus among those to be confirmed already.

Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney is one of the top names up for grabs in this year’s transfer window, meaning the end of a nine-year stint at Canyon-SRAM. The Pole is a former Tour de France Femmes winner who has proven her skills in both the Classics and Grand Tours and took the best victory of her career on Mont Ventoux at this year’s Tour.

However, Daniel Benson wrote on his Substack several months ago that Niewiadoma-Phinney could be on the move for 2027, with Lidl-Trek ‘on the verge’ of signing her to a three-year deal. The team were keen to sign a big-name leader having lost Elisa Longo Borghini two years ago. The deal has since materialised after one of the year’s worst kept transfer secrets.

Niewiadoma-Phinney isn’t the only rider set to shake up the team’s GC hierarchy. Felix Gall and Gregor Mühlberger have both penned deals with the men’s team, as has Jordan Jegat. These recruits have all shone at Grand Tours in 2026, offering Lidl-Trek some extra cards to play in stage races. The question now lies: are there too many cooks in the kitchen?

Confirmed: Fabio Jakobsen signs for Visma mid-season

After several years in the wilderness, Fabio Jakobsen has clarified his future as he announces a move to Visma-Lease a Bike with immediate effect.

The Dutchman moved to Picnic PostNL in 2024 after a big money deal was sealed with his previous Quick-Step team. He has underperformed since his first season at Picnic, when he took just one victory at the Tour of Türkiye. He hasn’t won since and has found himself out of WorldTour rotation.

Rumours first broke about a move this month, courtesy of Wielerflits. The move seemed odd, but the Dutch website made the observation that Jakobsen lives close to Mathieu Heijboer, Visma’s head of performance, with whom he has regularly ridden in the region throughout his career.

Some have speculated that Visma know something about Jakobsen’s numbers. The team could be hoping to hire a new sprinter after losing Olav Kooij last year, and with Picnic terminating his contract, it was a cheap, and therefore low-risk, move.

Jakobsen has signed with immediate effect on a deal that runs until the end of 2027. Can he turn his career around?

Confirmed: Paul Seixas is off the market, for now

The only rider seemingly capable of beating Tadej Pogačar in the near future is Paul Seixas. And after a season spent honing his craft as a stage racer and Classics rider, plenty of teams see him as the only logical transfer to make in the quest for Grand Tour glory.

Rumours first emerged in the spring, with UAE Team Emirates-XRG said to be in the mix. Since then, more teams have been linked to the French supertalent. Wielerflits reported last week that Visma-Lease a Bike had been in talks with Seixas, with team boss Richard Plugge admitting that the two had been in contact for the past year.

Pinarello-Q36.5 also emerged as a candidate with an offer that is said to be in the region of €13 million to €20 million – rumoured to be ‘the biggest contract ever seen in professional cycling’, according to transfer guru Daniel Benson. It’s worth noting that the squad, while on the ProTeam level, is backed by South African billionaire Ivan Glasenberg. His connection to Pinarello-Q36.5 – and financial stakes in both title sponsors – has often been regarded as a driving force behind these big moves.

At a post-Tour criterium, Paul Seixas clarified that he will not be switching teams: ‘Next year I’ll just be riding for Decathlon CMA CGM. For me that is a certainty, because I still have a contract until the end of 2027.’ Cue another summer of rumours then.

Confirmed: Alpecin-Premier Tech sign more sprinters

Alpecin-Premier Tech have continued to strengthen their position as a Classics and sprinting squad by announcing a trio of fast transfers. Madis Mihkels, Iván García Cortina and Casper van Uden have all signed to the Belgian squad with a similar goal.

‘We had profiles in mind for what we needed if we were going to lose riders in certain areas,’ team boss Philip Roodhooft explained, referring to the loss of Australian sprinter Kaden Groves. ‘We felt we were missing a rider who could compete in the finales and support Van der Poel. We needed to fill a gap with Cortina, and if you can also bring in someone like Mihkels, you shouldn’t hesitate.’

Alongside these transfers, an extension is expected to be announced for multi-discipline talent Tibor del Grosso, who has often been touted as the heir to Mathieu van der Poel’s spot within the team.

Confirmed: More losses at Picnic PostNL

Picnic PostNL have been struggling in 2026. Their season has been one of the weakest ever seen in the top division. That status has been accelerated by some big losses in the transfer market over the past few seasons, most notably Oscar Onley in last year’s transfer window. This year, the losses continue.

A wave of departures in the sprinting department have been confirmed. All the team’s former Grand Tour stage winners have left: Fabio Jakobsen, Casper van Uden and Pavel Bittner.

As Het Laatste Nieuws first reported, Casper van Uden, a stage winner at the 2025 Giro d’Italia, has signed a deal with Alpecin-Premier Tech, home to Jasper Philipsen and Mathieu van der Poel. The Dutchman is considered to be a replacement for Kaden Groves, who has long been rumoured to be leaving Alpecin-Premier Tech at the end of the season.

On the women’s team, Picnic have lost young talent Megan Arens with immediate effect. The Dutch rider, who won the world junior time-trial title last year, has been making waves in her neo-pro year, but her time with Picnic was cut short drastically, leaving the team within just eight months to go to AG Insurance-Soudal.

The team have been subject to some damning reporting by Dutch outlet NOS, which uncovered a ‘dictatorial’ culture within the team. The deadline for WorldTour registration has also elapsed and some believe the team will be forced to step down at the end of 2026.

Rumoured: Paula Blasi linked to four teams

Hot off a breakthrough spring in which she claimed Vuelta Femenina and Amstel Gold Race victories, Paula Blasi is said to be a key target for several teams in this year’s transfer window. The Catalan rider has been a force of nature in her year at the WorldTour level so far, but it looks as though her time with UAE Team L’Imad is reaching a crossroads.

According to Gazetta dello Sport, Blasi has been offered a three-year extension at UAE Team L’Imad, but this result is ‘unlikely’ – perhaps a sign of the team’s current overflow of GC contenders, including Elisa Longo Borghini, Dominika Włodarczyk and Pauliena Rooijakkers.

Instead, Blasi – who is claimed to have a €100k buy-out clause on her contract that currently runs through 2027 – has been approached by FDJ United-Suez, Uno-X, Lidl-Trek and Movistar.

In the lead-up to the Tour de France Femmes, the Movistar offer appeared to have been explored. According to Wielerflits, the Spanish squad is willing to fork out €1 million per year, which would make Blasi, who now has the same agent as Tadej Pogačar, one of the sport’s top-paid riders.

Confirmed: Arnaud de Lie to Tudor Pro Cycling

Former Belgian champion and WorldTour-winning sprinter Arnaud de Lie is expected to leave Lotto-Intermarché after four years with the team since he turned pro in 2022. This comes after a messy merger with Intermarché last year and a stagnation in results over the past 12 months.

De Lie was one of the fastest riders to secure a new deal for 2027. However, after months of build-up, it’s now been announced that De Lie will move to Tudor Pro Cycling on a lengthy four-year deal.

He joins Fabian Cancellara’s team as yet another sprinter to add to their artillery alongside Arvid de Kleijn, Luca Mozzatto, Matteo Trentin and another new addition Kaden Groves. That said, De Lie would spearhead the team’s Classics contingent, which enjoyed a strong spring this year.

According to previous reports from Het Laatste Nieuws, De Lie received interest from Groupama-FDJ United, Alpecin-Premier Tech, Soudal Quick-Step and Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe. However, the Belgian newspaper believes wage discussions became a sticking point at those teams and Tudor were reportedly the only team willing to foot the bill for De Lie, who demanded a higher salary than the one he’s currently on at Lotto-Intermarché.

Confirmed: Cédrine Kerbaol makes surprise move to SD Worx

After making a big splash in 2024 with her clandestine move to EF Education-EasyPost, French rider Cédrine Kerbaol is to leave the American team after two succesful seasons there.

Kerbaol finished inside the top ten at two Tour de France, and in the top five of the Vuelta. She’s become a consistent force in stage races, becoming one of France’s best climbers and time-triallists in the process.

However, this progression will now be under the hands of SD Worx Protime. The team have sometimes struggled to succeed in GC without Anna van der Breggen, so the move makes sense in that regard. The deal will last two seasons, with the team’s staff suggesting that she will be used with an angle toward her GC skills and attacking style.

Confirmed: Ineos’s transfers start to take shape

Netcompany Ineos are in the thick of a restructuring. The roster is changing shape quickly as the team prepare to head into their first full year with the financial backing of Danish AI tech firm Netcompany.

Gone is Sam Welsford, who moved to the squad just last year. The exit comes ahead of schedule, with Jayco-AlUla willing to foot the bill for the sprinter who only managed to score one win in 2026. That has left American versatile sprinter Riley Sheehan to jump on board along with British rider James Shaw, who may attempt to fill some of the domestique gaps left by the team’s list of departures, notably Ben Turner, who has gone to Soudal Quick-Step.

Harald Tejada has been announced as one of the incomers. The Colombian has been a staple of XDS Astana’s comeback over the past few years, with a stage win at this year’s Paris-Nice the highlight. Fellow Astana rider Clément Champoussin will also make the move to Netcompany Ineos in the winter.

As for young talent, Ineos have had some bad luck in the off-season with departures as AJ August, Magnus Sheffield and Artem Schmidt all jump ship.

In an attempt to off-set this, the team have picked up EF talent Markel Beloki. The Basque rider, son of Joseba Beloki, has been performing well over the past two years. In the summer, this translated to a first stage race victory at the Tour de l’Ain. Still just 21, Beloki could provide an interesting project for the years to come, especially alongside Spanish Junior World Champion Benjamin Noval, who’s expected to make the step up to the WorldTour in 2027.

As for young British talent, the team have poached 2024 Tour de l’Avenir winner Joe Blackmore. The former NSN rider has been out of action for most of 2026, but his previous results in both stage races and Classics paint a promising picture.

Rumoured: Chloé Dygert to leave WorldTour to focus on LA Olympics

Daniel Benson has reported on his Substack that two-time World Champion Chloé Dygert will be making a move away from the WorldTour this winter. This comes after a pair of frustrating seasons for the American, in which she suffered several injuries and setbacks, most recently with a DNF at Paris-Roubaix.

Her rumoured destination is Virginia’s Blue Ridge-TWENTY28, an American Continental team that seeks ‘to achieve long-term success for Team USA at the World Championships and Olympic Games’. The squad are one of the USA’s longest-running teams on the North American scene, having celebrated their 20th birthday this year. During that time, they have helped to foster 16 Olympic and Paralympic medalists and 17 World Championship titles. 

Dygert rode for the team before her WorldTour move, back when they were called Sho-Air TWENTY20. Even on the Continental level, Dygert took the team’s jersey to the top step of the road podium with her first time-trial world title in 2019 before doubling down on her responsibilities in the American team pursuit squad for the delayed Tokyo Olympic Games.

This 2027 move suggests that Dygert will be parking her WorldTour ambitions to one side until the 2028 Olympics, which take place in LA. She’ll likely be fielded alongside the reigning Olympic champion lineup in the team pursuit on the track, but she’ll remain eligible for the road races too.

Women’s transfer round-up

The women’s market has been fairly active in 2026. As mentioned, Lidl-Trek have been one of the busier teams. The newest signings Ally Wollaston and Blanka Vas will lend the team some big chances in the Classics.

Shirin van Anrooij tries to fill the void at Canyon-SRAM after penning a deal with the German team. Going the other way, Cecilie Uttrup Ludwig will head to Uno-X, where she’ll join Usoa Ostolaza, who signs after cracking the top ten at the Vuelta back in the spring.

Human Powered Health have been busy as well. The American team have been focusing on sprinters, with Amalie Dideriksen among a stellar list of signings that include Tour de France Femmes stage winner Yara Kastelijn and Letizia Paternoster.

FDJ United-Suez have also managed to bring in multi-discipline star Fem van Empel after some time away from the sport. This might be more of a cyclocross deal, given Van Empel was World Champion before bowing out the sport two seasons ago. However, the squad have been eager to bring more riders in from mixed-discipline backgrounds, including US champion Kate Courtney.

Otherwise, Pfeiffer Georgi has confirmed that she’ll be off to UAE Team L’Imad, marking another big departure for Picnic, time-trial prodigy Felicity Wilson-Haffenden backs Fenix over Lidl and Femke Markus places her trust in Visma going forward.

Men’s transfer round-up

There are a few confirmations on the men’s side that we haven’t had the chance to mention yet too.

UAE Team Emirates XRG have been quite quiet so far. Abel Balderstone, Marco Frigo and Pierre Gautherat are the only riders to have been wrangled in by the super team as of yet. Similarly, Visma-Lease a Bike have only revealed the transfers of Britain’s Mark Donavan and Fabio Jakobsen.

Mikel Landa has landed his final contract at the Euskaltel squad, meaning the Basque rider and recent stage winner at the Vuelta will be on the second division in 2027. Davide Ballerini, another recent Grand Tour stage winner, is also bound for a move to the second tier of pro cycling as he packs his bags for Pinarello Q36.5.

Elsewhere Guillaume Martin is set for a return to Lotto-Intermarché, Magnus Sheffield will get in touch with his Norwegian roots at Uno-X, while Tour de France stage winner Anthony Turgis has signed a new deal at XDS Astana.
